adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — tu` from `TopicUser.find_by` can be nil (no TopicUser row yet for this user/topic), causing `tu.notification_level` to raise NoMethodError instead of unsubscribing

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is used and then `tu.notification_level` is accessed immediately. There is no guard or fallback (e.g., `TopicUser.change`/create) if `find_by` returns `nil`, so a missing `topic_users` row would raise `NoMethodError` and break the unsubscribe flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6:5 — Unrelated var-to-const/function-shorthand reformatting bundled into the unsubscribe feature commit, unnecessarily widening the diff and review risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff for `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/topic-from-params.js.es6` includes refactoring unrelated to the unsubscribe feature: converting `model: function(p)` to method shorthand `model(params)`, changing multiple `var` declarations to `const`, and reordering declarations (e.g., introducing `const self = this` before the promise). This widens the PR surface area without functional necessity for unsubscribe, increasing review/merge risk even if behavior is intended to be unchanged.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/topic_user.rb:113 — Hash-brace/line reformatting of the MessageBus.publish call is a cosmetic change unrelated to the feature, mixed into the same commit as the behavioral change.

adjudication.rationale: The referenced change in app/models/topic_user.rb around the MessageBus.publish call is purely a whitespace/hash-brace formatting tweak (e.g., `{notification_level_change: ...}` to `{ notification_level_change: ... }`) with no behavioral impact. The finding is essentially a style/process nit about cosmetic changes, and the claim about being “mixed into the same commit” cannot be verified from a unified diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/views/email/notification.html.erb:1 — Whole-template indentation/erb-style reformatting (partial locals hash syntax, tag spacing) is mixed with the actual unsubscribe_link footer addition, obscuring the real behavioral diff.

adjudication.rationale:
In app/views/email/notification.html.erb the diff is essentially a reindent/reformat (Rails hash syntax, whitespace/line breaks) plus moving existing markup into a different indentation structure. The unsubscribe_link footer is not newly added here—it already existed in the old template (`
%{unsubscribe_link}
`). The actual new unsubscribe behavior is introduced elsewhere (server.en.yml adds a topic-specific unsubscribe link, message_builder passes unsubscribe_url), so the finding’s claim that a real unsubscribe_link footer addition is mixed into this template change is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:107 — tu` from `TopicUser.find_by` can be nil (e.g. user never tracked/visited the topic), causing NoMethodError on `tu.notification_level` and a 500 when a user clicks the unsubscribe link in an email

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` is used and then `tu.notification_level` is accessed unconditionally. `find_by` can return `nil` (no guard or `find_or_create_by`), which would raise `NoMethodError` and cause a 500 on the unsubscribe route.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:113 — tu.save!` raises ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid on validation failure with no local rescue and no visible rescue_from for it, turning a validation error into an unhandled 500 from an email-link click

adjudication.rationale: In the new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, the diff shows `tu.save!` with no local error handling (`rescue`) in that method. While `save!` can raise `ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid` if validations fail, the diff does not show TopicUser validations or any global `rescue_from`, so the claim that this will definitely become an unhandled 500 cannot be fully verified from the diff alone. However, using `save!` in a controller action reachable via an email link without handling failure is a concrete robustness concern grounded in the shown code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:94 — unsubscribe is a state-changing GET endpoint protected only by session cookie (ensure_logged_in), so it is forgeable via CSRF (e.g. an ) to silently change a logged-in victim's notification level for a topic

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action (app/controllers/topics_controller.rb) and maps it to `get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` and `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"` (config/routes.rb). The action changes server state by toggling `TopicUser.notification_level` and calling `tu.save!`. Since it is a GET endpoint, Rails’ CSRF protections generally do not apply, and it is only gated by `requires_login ... :unsubscribe`, making it forgeable via cross-site requests (e.g., an ``), as the finding describes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/topics_controller.rb:105 — tu` from `TopicUser.find_by` can be nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic, so `tu.notification_level` would raise NoMethodError; no test covers this edge case (untested nil path)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `TopicsController#unsubscribe` action, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return `nil`, but the code immediately dereferences it (`tu.notification_level > ...`, then assigns and `tu.save!`). The diff adds an email-level per-topic unsubscribe link (`unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`) which a user could click without ever having a `TopicUser` row for that topic, making this a real `NoMethodError` risk. No nil-guard or creation (`TopicUser.change`/`find_or_create`) is present in the diff.
